card.name: Link words after African-American authors
card.fires_on: Small linking or punctuation tokens right after the name of an African-American author or work, such as 's, a comma, and, from or as, in literature-syllabus text. The next word is expected to be a book title or another author.

modes.label: Possessive or link after author
modes.description: An 's, 'and', 'from' or comma follows an author's name, ahead of a title or another author.
modes.example: The first African-American novel published in the United States was Harriet Wilson<<'s>> Our Nig (1859

modes.label: Inside a work's title
modes.description: The pole fires partway through the title Our Nig, or at a quote mark opening a listed essay title.
modes.example: Our<< N>>ig is also a counter-narrative

card.writes: Promoted tokens are unrelated multilingual fragments and suppressed ones are scattered names, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It fires on small joining words after names like Du Bois or Washington in lists of African-American literature.
